title: Researchers develop Microdisk Laser Technology for faster AI chips
key_facts: Russian and Chinese researchers developed a method to optimize microdisk lasers that could help build photonic chips for AI and data centers.
The work involved HSE University in St. Petersburg and Qilu University of Technology's Laser Institute in China, published in the Journal of Lightwave Technology.
They measured a maximum -3 dB modulation bandwidth of 4.15 GHz in a 12-micrometer quantum-dot microdisk laser at room temperature.
They describe it as the first direct comparison of the laser's response under optical and electrical excitation.
The researchers say it could eventually let multiple circuits sit on one chip and enable optically linked microlaser networks.
quote_evidence: Their experiments showed a maximum −3 dB modulation bandwidth of 4.15 GHz.

The researchers said the ability to directly compare the laser's response under different excitation methods could help improve the design of photonic devices and accelerate the development of next-generation photonic chips.
why_it_matters_hint: A lab step toward light-based chips; no product or timeline.
